key_insight: In forced stably stratified turbulence, sharp density interfaces drift and merge when vertically-sheared helical structures emerge, while their absence leads to interface decay.
engineering_relevance: Understanding when stratified layers coarsen or remain stable is important for predicting mixing, transport, and layer persistence in geophysical and industrial stratified flows.
method: Direct Numerical Simulations of forced stably stratified turbulence
Long-time integration at moderate resolution to track slow coarsening
Compare regimes with and without vertically-sheared helical structures and relate helicity dissipation to buoyancy flux
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that at lower Fr=0.076, kinetic-energy excursions coincide with interface drift and merging, whereas at higher Fr=0.22 the interfaces mainly decay without the chiral structures.
watch_item: The conclusions come from moderate-resolution DNS in a specific forced SST regime, so quantitative thresholds for drift/merging may not transfer directly to other stratification strengths or forcing setups.
paper_title: Drift of interfaces in forced stably-stratified turbulence and the role of vertically-sheared helical structures
